hysteresis.headline: The next corpus wave should make hysteresis far more source-complete.
hysteresis.note: Until the 1892 paper is in custody, the page should keep using already processed books and lectures while marking the original law paper as the highest acquisition target.

complex-quantities.headline: The missing flagship is Steinmetz's 1893/1894 complex-quantities paper.
complex-quantities.note: The current page is grounded in processed textbooks; the proceedings paper will become the primary origin-point once scanned and sectioned.

symbolic-method.headline: The symbolic method needs its paper trail, not only later textbook treatment.
symbolic-method.note: Keep the 1897/1900/1916 AC editions visible as the book-development layer while the paper sources remain acquisition targets.

impedance.headline: Impedance will be strengthened by the complex-quantity and general-equation sources.
impedance.note: The current reader route remains the AC book editions and Electric Circuits; papers should not be cited as decoded until acquired.

reactance.headline: Reactance sits at the center of the next AC-method expansion.
reactance.note: Watch for how Steinmetz separates resistance, reactance, and stored-field exchange across editions and papers.

admittance.headline: Admittance should be connected back to the broader symbolic-method wave.
admittance.note: Parallel-circuit method is strongest in processed books for now; the new paper wave supplies origin and generalization once acquired.

transient-phenomena.headline: The next wave is especially strong for transients.
transient-phenomena.note: Use processed transient books now; pending articles will sharpen impulse, instability, gas discharge, and cumulative-surge layers.

lightning-surges.headline: Lightning and surge theory is the most urgent article-acquisition cluster.
lightning-surges.note: Keep existing surge statements grounded in processed transients until these articles have scan custody and equation review.

distributed-constants.headline: Distributed constants gain a much stronger line-and-cable route in the next wave.
distributed-constants.note: This should connect line theory, natural period, cable charge/discharge, and practical transmission systems.

electric-waves.headline: Electric waves should be expanded through line, lightning, and cable sources.
electric-waves.note: The current wave/radiation pages already help; the new sources will make circuit waves and line waves more precise.

dielectric-loss.headline: Dielectric and insulation language gets a stronger high-voltage path.
dielectric-loss.note: Treat breakdown and gas discharge as source-specific phenomena rather than generic dielectric mystique.

inductance-capacity.headline: Inductance and capacity connect directly to cable, line, and discharge sources.
inductance-capacity.note: This is a good reader doorway into distributed rather than lumped electrical behavior.

ether.headline: Ether remains a boundary topic, not a claim bucket.
ether.note: The new sources may enrich field-language context, but Wheeler-style or broader ether-field readings must remain labeled interpretation unless Steinmetz explicitly says it.
